Tamanna Yesmin Maria

For four days, a five-month-old infant with severe pneumonia was treated on the floor of a crowded regional medical college hospital because no paediatric bed was available.

Across district hospitals in Bangladesh, seasonal respiratory illnesses regularly push paediatric wards past two hundred percent of their designed capacity.

Doctors and nurses work exhausting shifts while families struggle to buy essential nebulisers and medicines from outside pharmacies.

Decentralising primary paediatric care to upazila health complexes can substantially reduce avoidable referrals to tertiary centres.

Budgetary allocations must prioritise infection control, oxygen supply lines, and trained neonatal nurses so every child receives dignified care.
